quick.topic: Give the reason with the design
quick.summary: Why I think it looks cleaner loses the argument, and what to say instead.
quick.takeaway: Decision, the evidence for it, and what you traded.

parts.title: Give the reason with the design

beats.line: I said the new layout looks cleaner. My manager prefers the old one. Now what?

board.text: Give the reason with the design

beats.line: Taste against taste. Nobody can win that.
Give a design rationale. Three parts.
Can I just call it the reason?
Yes. The reason. Still three parts.
The decision. The evidence behind it. And what you gave up.
I moved filters to the top. In testing, four of five missed them on the side.
The trade off is a little less room for results.
Now they can argue with evidence, not with your taste.

quiz.question: Which statement gives a design rationale?
options: I moved filters up because four of five testers missed them on the side.
I think this version looks cleaner.
This is how modern apps do it.
Trust me, this one is better.
quiz.explanation: It states the decision and the evidence behind it, which others can weigh.

quiz.question: Saying a design looks cleaner is enough to justify it to stakeholders.
quiz.explanation: That is taste. A rationale gives the decision, the evidence for it and what was traded off.
